steps.hints: ❓ What symbols are missing from the the nameList empty array declaration?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What symbols assign an initial value to an array and contain the elements in it?


Solution: 

= [] should be added to the end of the nameList array declaration code on Line 58.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the string “Daisy” is unable to be pushed to the nameList array.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the nameList declaration code includes the correct symbols to assign and contain the elements in its array.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Which function should be used so that users can submit strings?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What type of values should be pushed to the nameList array?


Solution: 

askForNumber should be replaced with askForString in the push function on Line 67.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Notice the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Line 67: the argument of type ‘number’ is not assignable to parameter of type ‘string’.



Fix the bugs in the code so that the 3 user submitted strings can be pushed to the nameList array

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about arrays and several functions available to help you create and update arrays in JavaScript. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Making a List, Checking it Twice
badges.description: Create and modify arrays within a program in JavaScript.

badges.title: Array of Sunshine
badges.description: Create an array in JavaScript.

badges.title: A Lengthy Calculation
badges.description: Calculate the length of an array.

badges.title: I Choose You!
badges.description: Access an element based on its index in an array.

badges.title: Objects May Be Larger Than They Appear
badges.description: Change the scale of a sprite.

badges.title: You’ll Fit Right In
badges.description: Use the push function to add an element to the end of an array.

badges.title: A String of Questions
badges.description: Use the askForString function to prompt the user for a string response.

badges.title: For Each Its Own
badges.description: Use a for element of loop to iterate through all the elements in an array.

badges.title: Search Engine
badges.description: Use the indexOf function to find the index of a provided value in an array.

badges.title: You’re Outta Here
badges.description: Use the removeAt function to remove a specific element from an array.
